investigate: Traditional, recipe-like laboratory practices have been criticised for offering ==limited cognitive engagement==.
The study compared the Science Writing Heuristic (SWH) with the ==Model-Based Science Writing Heuristic (M-SWH)==, which integrates modelling with argumentation and writing.
A quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test design measured the ==problem-solving perceptions== of 53 pre-service elementary teachers.
find: Both approaches had ==significant effects with large effect sizes== on the teachers’ problem-solving perceptions.
The M-SWH approach improved problem-solving perceptions ==significantly more== than the SWH-based approach.
The study may support integrating lab activities that combine ==argumentation, modelling and writing== into undergraduate programmes.

caption.question: Does adding modelling to laboratory writing activities change how future teachers see their own problem-solving?
caption.intro: Nejla Atabey compares the **Science Writing Heuristic** with its **model-based version** in laboratory activities for pre-service elementary teachers, using a quasi-experimental design.

source_notes.investigate: Background, Purpose, Sample and Design and Methods sections of the published abstract. 53 = 25 control + 28 experimental teachers analysed after data screening.
